item.title: Make listItems follow next_cursor
item.brief: Operator request: update inventory-client so listItems(transport) resolves to every item, in order, by following next_cursor from GET /items until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor. Update the README to document the change. Keep `npm test` passing and add tests for multi-page, single-page, and absent-next_cursor cases using the existing fake transport pattern. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

state.summary:
listItems in inventory-client now follows next_cursor from GET /items until it is null or absent, and resolves to all items in order. The first request sends no cursor; each later request sends the previous next_cursor unchanged as cursor. Changed files: client.js, test/client.test.js (three new cases: multi-page, single page with null next_cursor, single page with absent next_cursor, plus a check of the exact query sequence), README.md (documents the paging). Before: a two-page fake returned only page one ([{"id":1}]); after: both pages ([{"id":1},{"id":2}]). Checks: npm test exits 0 with 6/6 passing (baseline was 3/3). Committed locally as 67db554 under the repo's configured identity (mengsig); not pushed. Review: independent read-only reviewer agt_01M8AJNAG3FEHTZZZYB799NJ4G returned pass with no blocking findings. Open follow-ups (non-blocking): listItems has no guard against a server that repeats a cursor, which would loop forever; the README's "ordered by id" claim predates this change and is not enforced by the code or tests. No servers or processes were started, so nothing is left running.

pr.body: Approach: listItems loops over GET /items, building the query as {} for the first request and {cursor} afterwards, concatenating each page's items in order, and stopping when next_cursor is null or absent. An items array and a string-or-null next_cursor are asserted at each page. Files: client.js (listItems), test/client.test.js (multi-page, null next_cursor, absent next_cursor, exact query sequence), README.md (documents the paging). Checks: npm test 6/6 pass, exit 0 (baseline 3/3). Review: agt_01M8AJNAG3FEHTZZZYB799NJ4G, pass, no blocking findings. Follow-ups, non-blocking: (1) no guard against a server that repeats a cursor, which would loop forever; (2) README 'ordered by id' predates this change and is not enforced by code or tests. Assumptions: the server returns items in id order, as the shared contract states; the client keeps server order and does not sort.
pr.summary: listItems(transport) now returns every item, not just the first page. Before: only page one returned. Now: follows next_cursor until null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged; first request sends no cursor.
pr.title: listItems follows next_cursor across all pages

risk.why: Three small files in one client module; the only behaviour change is the documented pagination loop, and single-page responses behave as before. Tests cover multi-page, null and absent next_cursor. Reviewer confirmed low.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: Operator request: GET /items in inventory-api returns every item in one response, which no longer scales. Add cursor pagination per the shared contract: optional limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque, from a previous next_cursor). Body becomes {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}, items ordered by id, next_cursor null on the last page. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error": "..."}. Update the README to document the change. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing and add tests for paging, limits, and 400 cases. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

state.summary:
GET /items in inventory-api now does cursor pagination per the shared contract: optional limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque, the last id of the previous page as a digit string). Body is {"items", "next_cursor"}, ordered by id, next_cursor null on the last page. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400 {"error": ...}, including oversized digit strings (fixed after review). README documents it. Tests: `python3 -m unittest` passes, 11 tests (was 3), covering paging walk, exact-fill, past-end cursor, limit bounds, invalid cursor and oversized input. Committed locally as 3cdf9c6 on archon/zaeex1gp-add-cursor-pagination-to-get-items (base c36863e), not pushed. Review: first reviewer failed on an unbounded int() crash, fixed in 3cdf9c6; delta reviewer passed the head. Left open: the pre-existing get_item int(raw_id) on very long digit paths can still raise ValueError (non-blocking, outside this change). Also: default page size of 20 changes the GET /items response for existing callers, so the inventory-client sibling must follow next_cursor. No processes left running from this stage. Review: pass.
